clue.text: Still checked stuff after pocketing key

indicators.note: something pocketing an item holds it inside, so the fabric takes the key into its middle

parts.note: plaid is checked or tartan cloth
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone checks over their belongings after slipping a key into a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is only a link: PLAID, with 'pocketing' putting C inside it, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid water is calm and unmoving, so the word is a synonym of the adjective still.

indicators.note: not quite the whole word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: something stuck fast is locked in place

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain philosopher is almost, but not entirely, jammed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link; 'not quite' cuts the D from LOCKED.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was a seventeenth-century English empiricist thinker.

definitions.meaning: a bar of confectionery eaten as a snack
a warm cocoa beverage made from the same stuff

explanation.surface: A café counter serving warm beverages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snack bar' looks like a café, but it is a confectionery bar; 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The confection comes as an eating bar and, mixed with milk, as a warm cocoa beverage.

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone stripping in a newly built Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal on DUNDEE, a city in Scotland; the letters rearrange to give the verb meaning strip.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to lay bare or remove a covering, a synonym of the verb strip.

parts.note: prices that are down have been reduced, so cheaper
to wheel is to turn round

explanation.surface: A bargain-price wheel on sale during a slump.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic slump or fall is called a decline, the same noun sense.

clue.text: Certain object referred to in part of speech?

parts.note: certain means definite, sure
an article is an object or item

explanation.surface: A grammar question about some definite thing mentioned in a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'referred to in' is a link joining the wordplay to the grammatical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The' is called this in grammar, and articles are one of the traditional word classes.

clue.text: Campaign fund-one quarter cut by chief

indicators.note: a word cut by another is split open with the other placed inside

parts.note: west is one of the four compass quarters
arch means chief or principal, as in archenemy

explanation.surface: A political campaign's money is reduced by one quarter on the orders of its boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one quarter' reads as a fraction, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A store of money set aside for a political or business campaign is known by this name.

clue.text: Asian dog consuming a large number

indicators.note: a word consuming another swallows it, so the second goes inside

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail or follow them
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: A dog from Asia eating a great quantity of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is the verb meaning follow; 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamils are a people of southern India and Sri Lanka, hence Asians.

indicators.note: breaking things up puts their letters into a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Breaking in a politician's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking in' looks like horse training, but 'Breaking' shuffles IN plus SENATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocinante is the name of Don Quixote's horse in Cervantes' novel.

parts.note: a relation is a telling or narrative, an account
for can mean because of, owing to

explanation.surface: A relative is about to give an explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a family member, but it means a telling; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to give reasons for it, as in a phrasal verb meaning justify.

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken and the matching sound is entered

parts.note: gathered together means massed

explanation.surface: A kind of nut that is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beech and oak nuts lying on the forest floor are collectively called this.

parts.note: to behold is to observe or see
E and N are compass directions, east and north

explanation.surface: Someone required to watch where they are told to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beholden means owing a debt of gratitude, a synonym of obliged.

clue.text: Female ambassador gets bearings in American city

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: in places the bearings inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
E and N are compass bearings

explanation.surface: A woman diplomat finds her way around a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' looks like a description of the ambassador, but it is the definition, a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so a crossword can define it as a female.

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the run of words

explanation.surface: A fan names a favourite number by the composer Lehár.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehár was an operetta composer, which makes the definition fit the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo song is the dictionary sense.

indicators.note: something irrational lacks order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an argument that makes no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of logical thought put forward as a case is an argument.

indicators.note: in places the quiet sign inside the word for captured

parts.note: captured means taken
sh is a call for quiet
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense, captured city falls silent.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital of Uzbekistan in Central Asia.

clue.text: Family doctor never-not ever eats uncooked seafood

indicators.note: a word that eats another takes it inside

parts.note: kin are family
GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

indicators.note: not ever means the letters of ever are taken away

parts.note: taken as written before the cut
taken as written, then removed
raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: A family doctor never eats raw shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' reads as one GP but splits in two; 'not ever' leaves N from 'never'; 'eats' puts the uncooked word inside, before the final N.
explanation.definitionFit: A large prawn is shellfish eaten as food.

parts.note: dead can mean flat, as in a flat or dead battery
a heat is a race

explanation.surface: A tie between competitors in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead heat' is a tied finish, but here each word works alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race over level ground without jumps can be called a 'flat heat'.

clue.text: A note's concealed in exotic lilac flower

indicators.note: something concealed in another is hidden inside it
exotic means strange, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tune hidden within a foreign lilac bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges the shrub's letters to CLLIA, and 'concealed in' slips the A and the note in just after its first letter; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen shrub with showy blooms, related to the tea plant.

clue.text: Demand for energy included in retrospective study

indicators.note: included in shows one letter goes inside the other piece
retrospective looks backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a den is a study or private room
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A request for power in a review of a study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns DEN to NED, and E goes inside; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is a requirement or call for something, as is a demand.

parts.note: to sap is to weaken or undermine
PE is physical education, training
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A soldier's exercise run is undermined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. The question mark flags the definition by example: a sapper is a military engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a combat engineer in the army, so one kind of soldier.

explanation.surface: Wondering what happens after a very short spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of having' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both weight or importance and a very brief period.

clue.text: Organic compound child's taken from city

indicators.note: taken from means removed out of the other word

parts.note: Chester is a city in Cheshire, England
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A chemical compound belonging to a child is removed from a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry names a compound formed from an acid and an alcohol this way.

clue.text: Utensil for measuring soap out, wrapped in strange note

indicators.note: wrapped in shows one piece is enclosed by the other
strange means odd, so the letters are rearranged
out can mean amiss, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A measuring tool for soap, packed in an odd banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles the cleaning bar to ASPO and 'strange' turns the note to TEON; 'wrapped in' puts the first inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon is a standard measure of volume in cooking.

clue.text: Former union leader enters at the right moment

indicators.note: enters means goes inside the other word

parts.note: once means formerly

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A one-time trade union boss joins at just the right time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former union leader' looks like an ex-boss, but 'Former' is ONCE and 'union leader' is U.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre slang for coming in when signalled, so punctually.

indicators.note: in places the money symbol inside the word for model

parts.note: to model is to sit or pose for an artist
L is the abbreviation for pound, money

explanation.surface: Putting cash in a fashion model's keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' looks like a bank verb but is the noun; 'possession' backs up the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine sediment laid down by a river is a deposit.

definitions.meaning: acquiescence, putting up with what comes

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both welcoming approval and calm submission to fate.

indicators.note: heard means the words are spoken and we enter what they sound like

parts.note: to lament is to grieve

explanation.surface: Someone is upset on hearing a dirge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link, along with 'when'.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to distress or wrong someone, as upset does.

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ardent rebel lost their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Mad here is angry: someone who ranted went into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To rant is to rave angrily, so it fits going mad in the sense of anger.
